Working

1. Pipe velocity  
   A = πD²/4 = π(0.10)²/4 = 7.854×10⁻³ m²  
   V = Q/A = 0.025 / 7.854×10⁻³ = 3.18 m s⁻¹  

2. (a) Reynolds number  
   Re = ρVD/μ = (998)(3.18)(0.10)/(1.00×10⁻³) ≈ 3.18×10⁵  

3. (b) Darcy friction factor (Colebrook)  
   ε/D = 0.000046/0.10 = 4.6×10⁻⁴  
   1/√f = –2 log₁₀[ (ε/3.7D) + 2.51/(Re√f) ]  
   Iteration starting with Swamee–Jain estimate (0.0180) converges to  
   f ≈ 0.0179  

4. Velocity head  
   V²/2g = 3.18² / (2·9.81) = 0.517 m  

5. Major loss  
   h_f = f (L/D) V²/2g = 0.0179 (150/0.10)(0.517) = 13.9 m  

6. Minor loss  
   h_m = ΣK V²/2g = 5.5(0.517) = 2.84 m  

7. (c) Pump head  
   H_p = Δz + h_f + h_m = 12 + 13.9 + 2.84 ≈ 28.7 m  

8. (d) Shaft power (η = 0.72)  
   P_water = ρgQH_p = (998)(9.81)(0.025)(28.7) ≈ 7.03 kW  
   P_shaft = P_water / η = 7.03 / 0.72 ≈ 9.8 kW  

FINAL (a): 3.18e5 –
FINAL (b): 0.018 –
FINAL (c): 28.7 m
FINAL (d): 9.8 kW

I'm computing some final values. First, I multiply 0.24525 by 998, adjusting for minor differences, leading to approximately 244.76. Then, I calculate the hydraulic power by multiplying this by around 28.722, ending up with about 7,030 W or 7.03 kW.
